newsitem.title: USA: U.S. supermarket tabloid offers Cosby reward.
newsitem.headline: U.S. supermarket tabloid offers Cosby reward.

text.p: The U.S. supermarket tabloid, the National Enquirer, on Monday offered a $100,000 reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the killer of comedian Bill Cosby's son.
"Mr Cosby has been a long-standing friend of the Enquirer and the Enquirer's family of readers," the weekly newspaper said in a press release.
Ennis Cosby, a 27-year-old Columbia University graduate student, was shot dead Thursday while changing a tire along a freeway in the fashionable Los Angeles neighborhood of Bel Air.
Los Angeles police have been flooded with calls from the public in response to a composite drawing of a suspect, depicted as a white man in a knit cap.
"I urge anyone with any information about my son's death to come forward immediately," the Enquirer press release quoted Bill Cosby as saying.
The Enquirer, owned by American Media Inc, said people with information on the killing could call 1-561-540-1098 or 1-310-657-9872 or send e-mail to letters@nationalenquirer.com.
